content.text: @backend/src/helper/SystemConfig.class.php#L42-L59 What is the difference between self class and static class in this function?
I’ll inspect that helper and its nearby usage so the explanation matches this exact function, not just generic PHP terms.

In this function, `self::class` means exactly `SystemConfig`.

`static::class` means the class used at call time, via late static binding.

So here:

```php
property_exists(self::class, $propertyKey)
```

checks whether `SystemConfig` declares that static property.

But:

```php
new \ReflectionProperty(static::class, $propertyKey)
```

reflects the called class. If someone subclassed `SystemConfig` and called `ChildConfig::apply(...)`, then `static::class` would be `ChildConfig`.

In this codebase, there seems to be no subclass of `SystemConfig`, so `self::class` and `static::class` behave the same in practice. For clarity, this should probably use `self::class` in both places, because assignments also use:

```php
self::$$propertyKey = $value;
```

So the function is clearly writing to `SystemConfig`, not to subclasses.
